front: How long is an IPv6 address?
back: 128 bits: eight 16-bit groups. Each full group has four hexadecimal digits.

front: Why may an IPv6 address contain :: only once?
back: It represents omitted zero groups. Two occurrences make the number of zeros in each run ambiguous.

front: Which space is commonly allocated for global unicast?
back: 2000::/3. Having a global-form address does not itself prove Internet reachability; allocation, routes and policy also matter.

front: What is the ULA block and locally generated half?
back: fc00::/7 is ULA. Locally generated prefixes use fd00::/8, with a pseudorandom 40-bit Global ID. They are not intended for global Internet routing.

front: What is link-local scope?
back: The reserved block is fe80::/10; a normal link-local address has fe80 followed by zero prefix bits and its identifier. It is meaningful on one link and is not forwarded onto another.

front: Which multicast groups mean all nodes and all routers on a link?
back: ff02::1 is all IPv6 nodes; ff02::2 is all IPv6 routers. Multicast addresses are in ff00::/8.

front: How do you form a solicited-node multicast address?
back: Append the address's last 24 bits to ff02::1:ff00:0/104. For an address ending 12:3456, the group is ff02::1:ff12:3456.

front: What do ::1 and :: mean?
back: ::1/128 is loopback, the local node itself. ::/128 is the unspecified address, used when no source address is assigned in permitted initialization cases.

front: How is modified EUI-64 derived from a MAC?
back: Split the six MAC bytes after byte three, insert ff:fe, invert the first byte's U/L bit with XOR 02, and regroup into four 16-bit groups.

front: EUI-64 first byte: 00 becomes what, and 02 becomes what?
back: 00 becomes 02; 02 becomes 00. Invert the bit rather than always adding 2.

front: What does the A flag in an RA prefix-information option permit?
back: Autonomous address formation from that prefix when the other SLAAC conditions are met. It does not itself declare the prefix on-link.

front: Where does an automatically learned IPv6 default router come from?
back: A valid RA with a usable nonzero router lifetime. Its link-local source identifies the router; the host's address may separately come from SLAAC or DHCPv6.

front: What does ipv6 unicast-routing enable on a basic IOS router?
back: IPv6 forwarding. With enabled IPv6 interfaces and normal unsuppressed RA settings, it also lets the device operate as an advertising router. Addressing alone is not inter-interface forwarding.

front: ipv6 enable versus ipv6 address prefix/64 eui-64?
back: ipv6 enable supplies IPv6 processing and automatic link-local addressing without a global prefix. The eui-64 form also creates a global-form address using the supplied prefix and derived identifier.

front: How many /64 prefixes fit in a /56?
back: 2^(64 - 56) = 256. This counts subnets; do not subtract IPv4-style network and broadcast addresses.

front: What does a duplicate IPv6 address indication require you to investigate?
back: Another use of that unicast address on the local link. Exact duplicate labels vary by image; do not bypass the conflict check.

front: Is 2001:db8::/32 public Internet address space for deployment?
back: No. It is reserved for documentation. Use it in written examples and isolated labs, not as an assigned public production prefix.

front: Does assigning an IPv6 address automatically prove its prefix is on-link?
back: No. On-link information is separate from address assignment. RA prefix L flags and other explicit on-link configuration supply that information.

front: What does Duplicate Address Detection test?
back: Whether a tentative unicast address conflicts on its local link. A DAD NS can use the unspecified source ::. It does not check uniqueness across the entire Internet.

front: Two equally long zero runs: which does canonical IPv6 text compress?
back: The leftmost run. Canonical text does not compress a single zero group.

front: In a /61, how many low bits of the fourth IPv6 group lie outside the prefix?
back: Three. Clear those bits to calculate the containing prefix; a hex digit contains four bits.

front: What extra information makes FE80::2 a specific neighbor?
back: Its link or local exit interface. The same address text can exist on separate links.

front: What do the RA M and O flags describe?
back: M indicates managed address configuration; O indicates other DHCPv6 configuration. Neither flag supplies a DHCPv6 default-router option.

front: Can an RA provide a usable autonomous prefix but no default router?
back: Yes. A usable A-flagged prefix can remain valid while router lifetime zero excludes the sender as a default router.

front: Does an IPv6 /64 have an IPv4-style broadcast address?
back: No. IPv6 uses multicast for group delivery. Subnet counts do not subtract network and broadcast addresses.

front: Can two router interfaces use FE80::1 on different LANs?
back: Yes, because link-local scope is per link. Reusing an ordinary unicast address on the same link would be a conflict.
